A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, renamed from EnvInjection to WebInject. All 21 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original attack evaluations across ten webpage datasets and five MLLMs, with sensitivity studies, alternative-action results, and computational costs.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and the appendices.

M1.justification: WebInject is the renamed EnvInjection. Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same mapping network, differentiable resizing, constrained perturbation optimization, and webpage-source implementation.

E1.justification: Both evaluate real and synthetic webpages covering blog, commerce, education, healthcare, and portfolio domains. Monitor scenarios, semantically equivalent prompts, and alternative target actions are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Naive, Context Ignoring, Fake Completion, Combined, and Screenshot-based comparators. Their participation in the corresponding appendix comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 retains the same dataset counts, five MLLM configurations, monitor settings, generated prompts and histories, and ASR definition. The default perturbation bound of 16/255 and 2,500 optimization iterations are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both contain the same monitor-count and perturbation-bound sensitivity studies in Figures 2 and 11–14, perturbed-page examples in Figure 5, and alternative-action and paraphrased-prompt evaluations in Tables 10–11.

E5.justification: Both report ASRs averaged over webpages, prompts, and histories. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seed identifiers, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Matched numerical entries and plotted findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 reports Gemma-3 ASR of 0.972 for the proposed attack, 0.062 for the best webpage baseline, and 0.000 for the Screenshot-based comparator in both versions.

T1.justification: The threat assumptions, mathematical definitions, action-probability factorization, optimization formulations, and ASR equation are unchanged. Differences in extracted mathematical glyphs do not correspond to changes in the rendered equations.

C1.justification: Despite the shorter title and replacement of environmental-attack terminology, both versions claim an effective, stealthy, practical webpage perturbation attack against screenshot-driven web agents that outperforms existing baselines. The substantive contributions remain the same.

C2.justification: The explanations of attack effectiveness and monitor/perturbation sensitivity are retained. Section 8 preserves the source-code-access limitation, absence of closed-source transfer evaluation, and discussion of potential defenses.

D1.justification: Training details, including 16,240 mapping-network examples, 200 epochs, and batch size 16, are unchanged. The appendices retain the same pseudocode, implementation snippets, generation prompts, and NVIDIA RTX A6000 computational-cost information.

R1.justification: The referenced works and substantive prior-work comparisons remain unchanged. Section 1 adds another citation to Liu et al. (2024), which was already cited in v2; the renamed related-work heading does not change the discussion's substance.

P1.justification: v4 renames EnvInjection to WebInject throughout, shortens the title and abstract, and revises environmental-attack terminology and some introductory and concluding prose. Section order and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is enlarged, captions and table headings adopt WebInject, and the shorter title and revised prose cause local layout changes. All figures and tables are retained with the same scientific content.

improvement.justification: v4 mainly renames the attack, streamlines introductory wording, and adjusts presentation. The method, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations remain unchanged, with no meaningful net difference in the paper's overall quality.
